**Market believes:** Tencent is a recovering China internet conglomerate — gaming approvals have normalised, ad revenue is rebounding on AI-driven targeting, and the buyback programme provides a valuation floor. The investment portfolio is a mixed bag of stakes that may or may not unlock value. The stock is fairly valued, pricing in a mature, regulated platform with mid-single-digit growth.

**Why wrong:** The market conflates regulatory-cycle normalisation with secular platform deepening. Weixin's ad load remains "much lower than peers'" (management's own words) — this is not a recovery story, it is structural under-monetisation of a 1.4bn-MAU distribution platform. As Video Accounts, Mini Programs, and AI-targeted ads layer onto this base, revenue per user can compound at low-double-digits for years without aggressive ad-load increases. The market prices 8-10% growth; the platform can deliver 12-15% owner-earnings growth on a normalised basis once SBC moderates.

**What proves us wrong:** (a) SBC growth does not moderate — if SBC/revenue crosses 6%+ by FY27, the compounder is structurally broken regardless of top-line performance. (b) Ad-load expansion fails to materialise — if Marketing Services growth reverts to single digits for two consecutive quarters despite the AI targeting rollout, the monetisation headroom thesis is falsified. (c) Regulatory re-freeze — a new gaming license suspension materially impairs Domestic Games, the largest VAS profit driver.

**Market believes:** AMD is a losing NVIDIA-beta. The Q2'26 print (record revenue, DC +107%) still fell ~9% after hours because the Q3 guide "only" beat the published midpoint expectation, not the whisper — proof the multiple is stretched. MI400 is architecturally behind Blackwell/Rubin; ROCm will never match CUDA; ~80-85% NVIDIA accelerator share caps AMD.

**Why wrong:** Three primary-source facts the market mis-prices. (1) **The dated 2027 guide**: Su (Q2'26 call) guided DC revenue to "more than double" in 2027, growth "well above 100%," calling a ~$30B 2027 Instinct estimate "probably too low" — the market read the Q3 guide as a miss, ignoring that 2027, not Q3, is the story. (2) **MI450 is competitive on inference TCO**: 432GB HBM4 (vs Rubin R200's 288GB) fits a 405B-parameter FP8 model on one GPU; AMD claims Helios delivers up to +30% tokens/dollar vs Rubin NVL72. (3) **The TAM is expanding, not fixed**: hyperscaler capex ~$725B in 2026 (+77% YoY), ~$1T 2027E; OpenAI 6GW + Meta 6GW + Anthropic 2GW MI450 commitments scale AMD ~2x WITHOUT stealing NVIDIA share. The non-AI base (Client +23%, Embedded +19% at 40% op margin) is self-funding through the ramp.

**What proves us wrong:** MI450 independent benchmarks at TCO parity-or-worse; any named hyperscaler cuts 2027 capex; DC op margin compresses below ~27%; or Helios/MI450 revenue in the Q4'26 print lags the embedded ramp.

**Market believes:** NIM falls as cuts land, credit (card 3.34% NCO) is turning, and the 3.2x TBV premium is a peak-earnings trap — so JPM is a fade/short or, at best, fair-value with no upside.

**Why wrong:** The market mis-models NII as rate-elastic when the franchise has already repriced: H1-26 NII +9% with net yield ex-Markets down only 6bp through the delivered cuts (10-Q). Strip the one-offs and 1Q-2Q26 ROTCE is still ~23-24% vs 20-21% a year earlier — the premium is warranted, not euphoric. Residual income at COE 9.3% (UST10 4.77%, FRED 09-03 + USD ERP 4.5%), ROTCE ~20.5%, g 3.5% => warranted ~2.9-3.3x TBV; current ~3.16x is fair, so return is TBV compounding (~6%/yr) + 1.7% dividend + ~2.5%/yr buyback accretion, not de-rating.

**Market believes:** the -60%+ round-trip from the 2024 high reflects a structural break — Novo's obesity/diabetes near-duopoly is being dismantled by Lilly's oral and injectable competition, CagriSema's REDEFINE 1 data (22.7% weight loss) was a disappointment, and US pricing/political pressure (MFN, 340B, compounding) will impair growth and margins indefinitely, justifying a re-rating from a >30x growth multiple to a mid-teens "ex-growth pharma" multiple.

**Why wrong (partially):** the market is conflating a genuine, GUIDED, one-to-two-year PRICE/rebate-mechanics reset with a volume/demand collapse. Adjusted Diabetes care sales fell -12% CER in Q1 2026, but that is driven "mainly by lower realised prices" (MFN, gross-to-net normalization), not primarily by volume loss — while adjusted Obesity care sales grew +22% CER in the SAME quarter, with the newly-launched Wegovy oral pill already contributing DKK 2,256m in its first three months on the market [Q1 2026 announcement, "Adjusted sales" table]. CagriSema's 22.7% weight loss at 68 weeks beat semaglutide alone (16.1%) convincingly and was submitted to the FDA in Dec 2025 — a miss against an informally inflated ~25% bar, not a failed asset. Amycretin (Phase 3 obesity program starting Q1 2026, ~22% weight loss at 36wk in Phase 1b/2a) offers a second, underappreciated re-acceleration catalyst. Global GLP-1/obesity market penetration remains low relative to the eligible population, so the category is not shrinking — Novo's…

**Market believes:** Sony has completed its transformation into a content-and-recurring-revenue compounder, with PlayStation platform economics, music catalog scarcity, and a leading image-sensor position justifying a premium multiple. The SFGI spin-off simplified the structure, and the ongoing buyback signals management confidence in undervaluation.
**Why wrong:** The spin-off extracted the easy discount. What remains is governance-structural — cross-subsidization across segments, conglomerate overhead, and no pressure to break up further. Markets price buybacks at announcement, not at completion — the ¥500bn authorization is already in the price. Without a forward catalyst to unlock residual value, the discount can persist indefinitely. G&NS underlying OI is flat (the ¥57.2bn FX/impairment comparison padding masks this). I&SS faces discrete socket-loss risk, not a smooth fade.
**What proves us wrong:** (1) No further restructuring, spin-off, or activist pressure announced within 12 months — discount persists or widens. (2) Apple formally dual-sources image sensors, hitting I&SS revenue >15%. (3) G&NS OI declines as the FX tailwind and Bungie-impairment comparison benefits reverse in FYE-Mar-2027.

**Market believes:** The multi-year capex-driven margin/FCF trough (2023-2025) is over; the Feb-2026 Capital Management Day guidance (capex cut to $2-3bn, FCF/share target >$8) confirms an inflection, and TI deserves a re-rated multiple as a widening-moat 300mm-cost-position compounder — a view the market has already substantially acted on (+32%/12m, +67%/6m, screen row market-data snapshot).

**Why wrong:** We do not dispute the mechanism — it is real, filing-confirmed (Embedded op margin 6.2%→16.9% YoY in Q1'26 alone), and our own bottom-up build (constructed before viewing price) supports the DIRECTION of the consensus story. Where we differ is magnitude/price, not direction — that is a thin edge and we say so plainly. Running our own reinvestment-rate × ROIIC framework at a disciplined 9% COE and 2.5% terminal g (moat-adjusted slow fade to year ~15), fair EV/EBIT works out to **~12-14x**. At last price $311.46, EV (mkt cap $284.7bn + net debt $9.2bn = $293.9bn) is **~40x** our FY26E operating profit ($7,279m) and still **~29x** our FY29E operating profit ($10,187m) — a genuine, filings-derived gap, not a "feels expensive" comment, and one that persists even under our reasonably bullish forward margin path. The market may be paying for a longer/stronger fade than we think prudent, and appears to be underweighting that ~50% of TXN revenue ships into China (10-K geographic note) against the current "China weak/un-reflating" macro read…

**Market believes:** the FCF recovery is a one-time capex unwind; TXN is an expensive slow compounder with a disqualifying China overhang — the 7/13 valuation kill at $311 was fair, and the 12.6% pullback merely corrects froth.

**Why wrong:** the FCF inflection is structural, not a one-off. Capex is permanently ~10-15% of revenue (mgmt framework, 10-Q) after the 300mm buildout; CFO margin is a durable ~45% (8-K TTM). Q2'26 confirms with a primary print: TTM FCF $6.5B rising toward my $9.6/share FY26E (above the $8+ guide), Analog OM 45.6% (300mm cost moat widening, not peaking), inventory days 196 (channel clean). The market under-weights the AI analogue: data-center power grew ~90% YoY (dossier) — an AI-infrastructure franchise still priced like a cyclical. China is not yet the killer the prior kill assumed: Q2 China revenue +24% YoY to 22% of total, with no probe impact disclosed. At $272 the market pays ~28x FY26E EV/EBIT and ~30x FY27E EPS — a quality-compounder multiple, not a bubble, on a ~10% FCF grower at ~32% ROIC.

**What proves us wrong:** Q3/Q4'26 prints with FCF/share below the ~$9 run-rate; a MOFCOM preliminary dumping ruling with material share loss; inventory days breaking >250; or the FCF multiple compressing toward the DCF zone (~$120-150) — the $212 momentum-structure kill fires first on that last path.
excerpt.kill_criteria: Pullback resets entry $311→$272 (−12.6%). Q2'26 (8-K 7/22): rev +23% YoY, EPS $2.14 (+52%), TTM FCF $6.5B, Analog OM 45.6%, capex confirmed $2-3B, inventory days 196. **Market believes:** UNH is a sub-5%-margin insurer that "already recovered" (mom12 +40%); the 2025 earnings collapse was the first wave of a structural medical-cost problem, so the ~20x multiple is fair and the political overhang caps any re-rating.

**Why wrong:** The market prices UNH as a pure insurer, but ~60% of revenue and the growth engine is Optum (care delivery, pharmacy, data) — Optum H1'26 EFO $7,345M at 5.7% margin, up from 3.5% FY25. The 2025 collapse was a discrete MLR spike + cyberattack, not share loss. As MCR normalizes to ~88% (Q2'26 already 86.7%) and Optum Health margin recovers (4.9% H1'26 vs −0.3% FY25), EPS compounds ~9–10%/yr with a ≥$5B buyback. At 20x FY26E adj EPS the market pays a trough multiple for a recovering compounder — the derated_compounder_rerating pattern. DCF mid-case ~$479 (COE 9.5%, growth fade 10%→4%, terminal g 4%) vs entry $396 = ~17% discount.

**What proves us wrong:** MCR re-accelerates above ~89% (medical-cost inflation returns); Optum Health margin stalls below ~4%; UHC membership attrition accelerates (already −525K sequentially in Q2'26); or a structural MA Star Ratings revenue cut compresses the multiple below ~16x.

**Edge taxonomy:** analytical (primary — market mis-models the mix, pricing UNH as an insurer rather than a health-services compounder where Optum is the growth engine) + time-arbitrage (market can't hold a 3y MCR-normalization + Optum-margin-recovery view through political/regulatory noise).

The dividend is not the risk the market prices: it was covered 1.37x by FCF in the weakest cash year of the window (FY25) and XOM has not cut it in 40+ years; the flexible buyback — not the dividend — is the shock absorber in a downturn. At ~14x FY26E and ~10x through-cycle EBITDA, the equity prices the windfall but not the compounding, and a fortress balance sheet means the "Brent collapses and the dividend breaks" tail the market leans on has no balance-sheet mechanism behind it.

**What proves us wrong:** Brent durably below ~$81.5 (macro review marker), a dividend cut, a Permian decline or Guyana FPSO slip, or a buyback suspension that reveals the program was not FCF-durable.

**Market believes:** JSMR is a stable, state-backed toll-road compounder with an expanding 1,736km network, mechanical inflation-linked biennial tariff resets, and improving leverage post-JTT stake sale — a bond-proxy with growth optionality in Indonesia's infrastructure buildout.

JSMR's Rp10.6tn floating-rate bank debt reprices quarterly while biennial tariffs reset on 2-year lagged CPI — BI's defensive hiking cycle (5.75%, chatter to 6%) compresses real AFFO faster than tariff resets can recover it. This is exactly the archetype's dominant failure mode, not a future tail risk. The JTT stake sale ceded 35% of permanent toll cash flows without fixing the structural mismatch — deleveraging was cosmetic, not organic. Best-effort AFFO cannot clear the 10y FR 7.26% hurdle.
